extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Popular Science Monthly; educated public and students of social theory/sociology
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting the set of defining traits and normative claims Herbert Spencer gives for the 'industrial type of society' in his 19th-century essay; this is an analytic/descriptive framework for recognizing or comparing social types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: industrialism is not industriousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrialism must not be confounded with industriousness; the industrially-organized society is defined by the form of cooperation under which labors are carried on, not by the quantity of labor done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spencer gives examples: small societies with little exertion may be industrial in form; conversely, militant societies (ancient Egypt, Peru) could have immense labor yet not be 'industrially organized' because work was done under command and without private claims to products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: industrialism is not compulsory/communistic cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: The industrial type is distinct from systems where individuals are prevented from independently occupying themselves, competing, or hiring themselves on chosen terms (i.e., socialist/communistic compulsory cooperation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spencer argues that any artificial regulation preventing individuals from making their own engagements amounts to dictation similar to militant control; he notes communistic forms have existed in warlike societies and that communistic projects often originate in more warlike societies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradual and indistinct emergence of industrial structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Structures proper to the industrial type do not appear suddenly in distinct forms but begin in vague, unsettled gradations as modifications of preexisting (often militant) structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: transition from slave labor to free detached labor; change from presents to fixed wages; barter beginning as gift-exchange before definite equivalence and fixed prices develop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary requirement shifts from corporate action to maintenance of individual lives
rubrics_metrics.description: Where danger from external foes ceases, the society's chief requirement becomes sustaining itself by subserving the lives of its units (self-sustentation/multiplication of units) rather than corporate (war) action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private individuals may maintain themselves, exchange products, enter undertakings without direction of society as a whole; public action remains mainly to keep private actions within due bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense of individuality as cardinal state duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the industrial regime the society must defend each citizen's individuality — securing life, liberty, and property — rather than sacrificing individualities for corporate ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spencer claims industrial societies will protect personal rights so that individuals prosper; by survival of the fittest, societies that better maintain individual claims will outcompete others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Despotic/autocratic control excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: A despotic controlling agency is unnecessary and incompatible with the industrial type because autocracy restricts individualities which industrialism requires to have fullest play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spencer reasons an autocratic ruler, by mere presence and potential power, restrains citizens more than mutual limitation would; thus industrial societies favor non-despotic rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative agency for ascertaining and executing the average will
rubrics_metrics.description: Control required under the industrial type should be exercised by an appointed representative agency able to hear representatives of diverse interests and adjudicate openly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spencer contrasts a single arbitrator (private statements) with representative assemblies where cases are stated publicly and judgments follow general consensus; the latter is more congruous with industrial individualities and balances class-interests better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration is negatively regulative (limiting aggression) rather than positively prescriptive
rubrics_metrics.description: Public control in industrial societies issues mainly prohibitions ('Thou shalt not') rather than commands ('Thou shalt do this'); government imposes restraints only to check aggression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because citizens voluntarily cooperate for a public protector, they authorize it only to impose restraints they all have interest in maintaining; exceptions are criminals, who under peaceful conditions are few.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice defined as preservation of normal connections between acts and results
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice means obtaining by each as much benefit as his efforts are equivalent to — neither more nor less; public action should not abstract earned advantages to give to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spencer uses this to argue against communistic redistribution and in favor of contract: superior should have the good of his superiority; inferior the evil of his inferiority; public action should not award unearned advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: The universal relation of contract
rubrics_metrics.description: In the developed industrial type the relation of contract becomes general and ultimately universal, replacing status; exchanges and relations are governed by voluntary agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As militancy declines and industrialism rises, authority decreases and uncontrolled action increases; contract administered equitably yields apportioning of reward to merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of communistic public distribution from developed industrial type
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms of communistic distribution are incompatible with the developed industrial type because they tend to equalize the lives of good and bad, idle and diligent, undermining survival of the fittest in industrial struggle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spencer argues that societies allowing superior individuals to retain proceeds will produce more and better offspring and thus thrive over societies practicing enforced redistribution; private voluntary charity is not negated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralization and narrowing of public administration
rubrics_metrics.description: With industrialism, many public organizations disappear; administration becomes decentralized and narrowed primarily to administering justice and preventing aggression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spencer lists public services that would disappear or be reduced (compulsory schooling, state priesthood, state inspections, state-funded amenities) because they trench on individualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplicity and heterogeneity of private associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Private organizations — religious, commercial, professional, philanthropic, social of all sizes — proliferate to fill spheres vacated by diminished public agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The principles of voluntary cooperation and representative constitutions apply both to private combinations and to the representative constitution of the public; private associations are congruous with industrial organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative plasticity and social mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: The industrial type tends toward plasticity: social organization is easily modified; places and occupations are determined by efficiency rather than inheritance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without the status relation that fixes men in positions, changes of structure follow when men acquire functions for which they are most fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tendency toward loss of economic autonomy and greater interdependence
rubrics_metrics.description: Peaceful relations and industrial specialization reduce self-sufficingness; localities and nations become mutually dependent through advantageous exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spencer extrapolates that as war decreases, divisions between nationalities break down and common organizations (federations) may form; yet citizens will tolerate no restraints on exchange that trench on individualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical indicators: diminution of status, increase of contract, and protection of individual rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence for movement toward industrial type in civilized societies includes decrease of status (serfdom, rigid ranks), increase of voluntary cooperation and contract, less centralized autocratic rule, and more state protection of individual rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spencer contrasts medieval Europe (high militancy, enforced subordination) with modern times (less frequent wars, larger productive population working for its own benefit, representative institutions).
